svg.title: Stage 2 sequence diagram - Use case: a VIP customer from arrival to payment

g.text: Stage 2 sequence diagram - Use case: a VIP customer from arrival to payment
(Base setting, tests/victory.txt, turns 4 to 8 shown, then the result check)
- Customer 1 (Regular) is EATING at Table 1 (served on turn 3).
- Table 2 is free. No orders are waiting for the Chef.
- Customer 2 is scheduled to arrive this turn as a VIP (Stage 2 line-up).
Outcome: customer 2 pays $13.50 on turn 8 with satisfaction 90;
after turn 18 the game ends in VICTORY (5 paid, revenue $73.50, avg satisfaction 75.6).
Turn 4: customer 2 arrives and the Waiter seats them
[choice = Wait (manager choice that changes the outcome)]
c2 stays QUEUED and keeps losing 5 per turn,
so it is served later and pays with lower satisfaction
[invalid choice, e.g. no free table or wrong id]
customer 1 becomes READY_TO_PAY (calls as in turn 7)
Turn 5: customer 2 orders, the Chef cooks, customer 1 pays
no arrival this turn; staff resetTurn() as in turn 4
the customer chooses, never the manager.
VIP keeps the inherited rule; CriticCustomer overrides
locked into priceCents when the order is taken.
The Waiter already acted, so o2 can be served
[Chef choice = Wait (manager choice that changes the outcome)]
o2 stays PLACED, so it cannot be served on turn 6;
c2 waits another turn and loses 5 more satisfaction.
Turn 6: the Waiter serves the READY order
customer 3 arrives and is seated (same calls as turn 4)
the Cashier ran before this step, so c2 pays next turn at the earliest
Turns 9 to 18: the other customers follow the same pattern
[paidCount >= 4 and revenue >= 4500 cents and average satisfaction >= 60]
